item.title: The Slow Ledger of Things I Own
item.description: 30-second summary: A bone-conduction headset died after almost three years, and I wanted to know whether it had been worth buying. That question exposed a gap: I had never systematically recorded any durable thing I owned. So I built a small site that starts with an Excel sheet and derives service life, daily cost, cost per use, and retirement reasons, then turns the collection into a timeline. The public record now contains 69 items, with another 4 deliberately hidden; the items still in service add up to about ¥70.41 per day on today’s amortization basis. The number does not tell me what I should buy. It makes me see that an object’s value is made in all the ordinary days after it is bought.
